scenario: btrfs subvolume mount at /home whose single listed uuid has the qgroups directory present (initialized) with qgroups_enabled null (unreadable/invalid) and qgroups_mode null

fixture.mountinfo:
25 30 0:30 / / rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache,subvolid=257,subvol=/
26 25 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache,subvolid=256,subvol=/@home
27 25 0:31 / /proc rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:5 - proc proc rw
28 25 0:32 / /sys rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:6 - sysfs sysfs rw
29 25 0:33 / /tmp rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime shared:8 - xfs /dev/mapper/data rw,attr2,inode64,noquota

rationale: preseal-amendment.md §C2 final rules (btrfs bullet) plus the kernel sources: mount resolution (amendment, 'Mount resolution' bullet): the fixture mountinfo is parsed per proc.rst §3.5 field layout [S082]; candidate covering mountpoints for realpath /home/quota/unknown are '/' and '/home'; the longest component-prefix wins and neither covering mountpoint occurs more than once in the file, so the ambiguous_overmount refusal does not apply, and the trailing empty line is ignored. The chosen line '26 25 0:30 /@home /home rw,relatime shared:1 - btrfs /dev/mapper/root rw,space_cache,subvolid=256,subvol=/@home' is parsed by its separator and its last three fields, giving fstype 'btrfs', source '/dev/mapper/root' and super options 'rw,space_cache,subvolid=256,subvol=/@home'; no backslash escapes occur, so no escape rejection. Device gate (amendment, 'Device mismatch PREEMPTS the filesystem table' bullet): the chosen fstype is btrfs and the path's stat major is 0 (st_dev 0:58, the anonymous btrfs subvolume device, S081 = fs/btrfs/inode.c, inode.c:8246 'stat->dev = BTRFS_I(inode)->root->anon_dev'), so the btrfs equality skip applies and the mismatch against the mount major:minor 0:30 does not preempt the filesystem table. Device-to-uuid resolution (amendment, 'Fixture source resolution'): the raw decoded source '/dev/mapper/root' is looked up in device_links and yields the mapped basename 'dm-0', which is compared against the uuid records' devices lists; exactly one record lists 'dm-0', so the zero/multiple-match refusal does not apply. Quota classification (amendment, btrfs bullet): the qgroups directory is present (qgroups true, i.e. initialized) and qgroups_enabled is null, which the amendment defines as an unreadable or invalid enabled attribute, so the row 'Present plus enabled=null (unreadable/invalid enabled) -> unknown/n/a/btrfs_qgroups_enabled_unavailable' applies, giving quota_state 'unknown', enforcement 'n/a', basis 'btrfs_qgroups_enabled_unavailable'; this is deliberately distinct from the absent-directory row btrfs_qgroups_dir_absent, which the amendment allows only on a successful parent inspection, and it must never be reported as disabled. qgroups_mode is null because real mode reads qgroups/enabled first and reads mode only when enabled is exactly 1, so with enabled null the mode attribute is not consulted at all; the kernel's mode reader is guarded by ASSERT(btrfs_qgroup_enabled(fs_info)) and therefore yields no trustworthy mode text in this state [S079 = fs/btrfs/sysfs.c, qgroup_enabled_show reports the BTRFS_QGROUP_STATUS_FLAG_ON bit as an exact 0/1 and qgroup_mode_show emits 'qgroup' or 'squota' only under that guard]. The directory's existence is the initialization artifact of btrfs_sysfs_add_qgroups, created when qgroup support is first brought up and removed by btrfs_sysfs_del_qgroups [S080 = fs/btrfs/qgroup.c, call sites qgroup.c:441 and :1032 for add, :620, :689 and :1295 for delete], so directory presence and the enabled attribute are distinct facts and presence alone cannot settle the state. Verdict (amendment, output/verdict section; precedence unchanged): the single path is unknown with no enabled sibling, so exit 2 and finding_id 'QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN' (the setup-error class also exits 2 but is distinguished by finding_id QUOTA_SETUP and by producing paths=[] with a fixed error token; this case produces a classified path tuple, so it is not a setup error). Fixture-format conformance (amendment, 'Paths', UUID and record rules): the path is nonempty, unique, normalized and absolute with no dot/dotdot components, st_dev '0:58' is canonical decimal MAJ:MIN, the UUID key is canonical, the device basename 'dm-0' is a plain nonempty basename, and the uuid record carries exactly the keys devices, qgroups, qgroups_enabled, qgroups_mode with bool / bool-or-null / mode-or-null types (qgroups_enabled null is an allowed value, not a missing key). The btrfs super options carry no quota key, so quota_option_keys is empty by the amendment's btrfs rule.
